title: fix(app-shell,plugin-designer): standard nav entries are stored label-less, never with the target's machine name (objectui#11201, stage 1)
body:
Part of #11201
Clause-②: no

Stage 1 of ruling B on objectui#11201 (triage record `5910404448`, execution note `5910537969`). The card stays open: stage 2 is routed by triage on the census below. This PR does not touch the renderer's `isCustomized` guard in `resolveNavItemLabel`, and it does not touch `/meta`'s `translateApp` or the inline locale map.

## What changes

Ruling B keeps one rule, the spec's: a present `label` renders verbatim, and an absent one inherits its target's current label at render time, which is the text that localises. Step 1 asks every objectui producer to write a standard entry with no label, never the target's machine name. On `main`, the console's navigation sync already did (objectui#9868). Three other producers did not. They wrote the target's own text, which is its machine name for a draft or unlabelled object:

| Producer (symbol, file) | Wrote before this PR | Writes now |
|---|---|---|
| Console navigation sync: `NavigationSyncEffect` calling `syncPageCreated` / `syncDashboardCreated` (`newPageNavigationItem` / `newDashboardNavigationItem`, `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavigationSync.ts`) | no label since objectui#9868 (PR #11186, `a8198de22`). From the hook's first commit (`7c788f5de`, 2026-02-23) until then: `label: label \|\| pageName` / `label \|\| dashboardName` | unchanged. New pin: the stored entry renders its target's localized label under en and zh-CN |
| Public `syncPageCreated` / `syncDashboardCreated` / `…AllApps` with an explicit label | the author label verbatim. No in-tree caller passes one (the effect above is the only caller) | unchanged |
| Studio Create app with "add objects": `buildAppSkeleton` (`studio-design/skeletons.ts`) fed by `loadPackageObjects` (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) | `label` = the object's label, or its machine name for a draft object (`d.name`) or an unlabelled one (`o.label ?? o.name`) | no `label` key. The seed is names only |
| Studio nav-item panel, binding an object to a placeholder entry: `StudioNavItemInspector` (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) | replaced the placeholder with the object's label (`o.label ?? o.name`, so the machine name for a draft or unlabelled object) | removes the placeholder `label` key. A typed label and a locale map are kept as authored |
| App wizard: `generateNavFromObjects` (`plugin-designer/src/AppCreationWizard.tsx`), fed by `CreateAppPage` / `EditAppPage` with `label: obj.label \|\| obj.name` | `label: pluralLabel \|\| label`, so the machine name for an unlabelled object | a `label` only for a declared plural label that differs from the object's label and from its machine name (trimmed, case-insensitive): inheritance cannot produce a plural. Otherwise no `label` key |
| Navigation Designer quick add (`newNavItem`), Studio canvas "Add nav item" (`AppNavCanvas`) with `AppNavInspector`'s target picker | a placeholder (`New TYPE` / `New item`), never the target's name | untouched: not a machine-name producer, and objectui#11196 / PR #11207 hold these files |
| `DashboardDesignPage`'s `label: dashboardName ?? ''` (named in the dispatch as a lead) | not a nav entry: it is the dashboard document's own seed, on a not-found branch that returns before anything is saved | n/a |

Display: the sidebar renders each new label-less entry with the text the old stored copy showed, and additionally in the viewer's language and after a rename. Pinned under en and zh-CN below.

## Serial constraint: land after objectui#11196

objectui#11196 (this seat, branch pushed, no PR yet) makes the designer surfaces draw a label-less entry through the runtime's rule: the app preview, the Studio nav canvas and inspector, the Studio Interfaces rail, the Navigation Designer and the app wizard's Navigation step. Until it lands, such an entry shows as `Item N` on the Studio nav canvas and as a blank row in the wizard's Navigation step. This PR makes Create app, the bind and the wizard write such entries. Both branches edit `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, in different hunks: objectui#11196 edits the rail's `NavTree`, this PR edits `loadPackageObjects` and `StudioNavItemInspector`. `git merge-tree --write-tree` reports no conflict against objectui#11196's head `2a6f0c5fb` or against `main` `e6bc087a3`. No write site sits inside objectui#11196's hunks.

## Pins

- `useNavigationSync.standardEntryLocalizes-11201.test.tsx`: the real `NavigationSyncEffect` stores a new dashboard's entry with no `label` key. That stored entry is then rendered by `NavigationRenderer`, wired as `UnifiedSidebar` wires it (the `useObjectLabel` resolvers plus `useNavTargetLabel`), under a real `I18nProvider` carrying a zh-CN bundle loaded the console's way. It shows `Pipeline Health` under en and `管道健康` under zh-CN.
- `StudioDesignSurface.standardNavEntries-11201.test.tsx`: seeded entries carry no `label`, the app parses through the spec's `AppSchema`, and the stored entries render `Account` under en, `客户` under zh-CN, and `draft_thing` for the unlabelled object. Binding an object to a `New item` placeholder leaves no own `label` key, and the entry parses through `NavigationItemSchema`. Controls: a typed label is kept (a locale map is already pinned by the objectui#11148 test).
- `AppWizard.standardNavEntries-11201.test.tsx`: drives the real `CreateAppPage`. The unlabelled, singular-labelled and plural-equals-name objects' entries carry no `label`. Control: a distinct declared plural (`Accounts`) is written.
- `createConformance.test.ts`: the nav-seeded skeleton case now passes name-only seeds.

| D | bind: the placeholder removal deleted | 2 red: both placeholder-bind cases |

## Acceptance notes

### Census (step 2), reported before any conversion

Scanner: a TypeScript-AST walk of every `navigation: [...]` literal and its `children`, applying the guard's own test (plain-string label, trimmed and lower-cased, equal to `viewName` for an object entry naming a view, else `objectName`; `dashboardName` for a dashboard entry). The population was enumerated from the same ref it reads (`git grep` at objectstack `origin/main` `1741c5dcb`), and cross-checked by a second enumeration (`App.create(` and `: App =`), which found the same seven files. The matcher's own control is the one hit it reports.

| Population | Nav entries | Entries the guard reads | Label equals the target's machine name | Writer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| objectstack examples: crm, multi-package, showcase, todo | 76 | 33 | 1: todo `nav_overdue`, label `Overdue`, `viewName: 'overdue'` | author |
| objectstack platform apps: account, setup, studio | 49 | 6 | 0 | author (platform source) |
| objectstack scaffolds: `create-objectstack` blank template (no app), `objectstack generate app` (writes `Title` + `s` for the object) | 0 / 1 per app | 1 per app | 0 (the generated plural never spells the snake-case name) | author (a file the author owns) |
| objectui console preview fixture (`preview-samples.ts`, not stored) | 7 | 3 | 0 | fixture |
| page / report entries in the above, label against `pageName` / `reportName` (the guard does not read these) | 29 | not read | 0 | author |
| Stored app navigation in production | NOT MEASURED: needs production data | | | |
| A seeded console | NOT MEASURED: not booted. A fresh seed stores the packaged apps counted above, and the sync writes nothing without user CRUD | | | |

Split by writer, what is readable here: platform sync 0 (it writes only into stored rows at runtime; 0 sync-shaped ids in any source), `apply_blueprint` NOT READABLE (the `objectstack-ai/cloud` repo answers 403 through the proxy), author 1. `apply_blueprint`'s declared contract is readable: `BlueprintNavItemSchema.label` in `@objectstack/spec` says "Nav entry label (defaults to the target label/name)", so the applier is declared to store the target's label or name when a blueprint omits one.

**Can a stored row tell the writers apart?** Not from any recorded provenance. Partly from signatures and history:

- Per entry: nothing. A nav item is a strict object with no room for a mark, and the spec's describe says "No stored inherited flag".
- Per row: `sys_metadata`'s `source`, `managed_by`, `created_by`, `updated_by` and `version` describe the whole app document's last write, not an entry.
- Sync signature (strong, but a heuristic): the sync has always written id `nav_page_` or `nav_dash_` followed by a 13-digit epoch-ms stamp and a counter, with icon `FileText` or `LayoutDashboard`, and until objectui#9868 the page's or dashboard's machine name as the label. The shape is the same from `7c788f5de` to `a8198de22`. An author would have to type the timestamp id by hand.
- Weaker signatures: the Studio scaffold's id is `nav_` plus the object name (since `7a6837cfa`, 2026-07-05). A Studio-canvas entry's id is `nav_item_N`. The wizard's id equals the object name. Authors write ids like these by hand.
- History: `sys_metadata_history` keeps a full snapshot per version (`operation_type`, `source`, `recorded_by`, `change_note`), so diffing versions finds the write that introduced an entry. But the sync, the Studio and the wizard all save through the same `saveItem('app', ...)` door as the signed-in user, so those columns do not separate them. `sys_metadata_commit` (ADR-0067) groups AI-turn writes (`actor`, `ai_model`, an event range), so blueprint writes are attributable if the cloud applier writes through commits (not readable) and history is retained (not measured).

### Twin check (step 3): no

objectstack `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` at `origin/main` `1741c5dcb`, `translateApp`'s node walk:

```ts
if (typeof node.id === 'string') {
  const translated = lookupNavLabel(bundle, appName, node.id, opts);
  if (translated) next.label = translated;
}
```

`lookupNavLabel` reads only `apps.APP.navigation.ID.label` down the locale chain. Nothing compares a label's text with `objectName`, `viewName` or `dashboardName`, so it is not the equal-to-name rule. One observation for triage: it also gives a label-less node the bundle text when an entry exists for its id, ahead of inheritance, while the execution note orders the id-keyed bundle only for a present label. The CLI's extractor (`walkNavigation` in `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts`) emits such keys only for a present label, so only a hand-written bundle entry reaches this path.

### Noted, not filed

- The app wizard's Navigation step: objectui#11196's read (`resolveNavItemLabel(item)` with no target resolver) shows `objectName` for a label-less generated entry, though the wizard holds each object's label in `availableObjects`. This lies in that branch's hunk.
- `StudioNavItemInspector`'s Label input writes `label: ''` when emptied (`renamedLabel` with an empty value), and shows no inherited text as a placeholder. objectui#11196's `clearedLabel` handles `AppNavInspector` only. Read from the code, not measured.
- `AppNavInspector`'s target picker keeps `AppNavCanvas`'s `New item` placeholder as a present label. Both files are held by objectui#11196.
- The wizard's declared-plural copy is a present label: it does not localise or follow a rename, because inheritance has no plural rung. No carrier.
